import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Reed's omega, delta, and chi conjecture

*References*:
- [B. Reed,  ω Δ and χ, J. Graph Theory 27 (1998) 177-212.](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/(SICI)1097-0118(199804)27:4%3C177::AID-JGT1%3E3.0.CO;2-K)
- [openproblemgarden](http://www.openproblemgarden.org/op/reeds_omega_delta_and_chi_conjecture)
- [mathoverflow/37923](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/37923) asked by user [Andrew D. King](https://mathoverflow.net/users/4580/andrew-d-king)
-/

open scoped Finset

namespace ReedOmegaDeltaChi

/--
For a graph $G$, we define $\Delta(G)$ to be the maximum degree, $\omega(G)$ to be the size of the
largest clique subgraph, and $\chi(G)$ to be the chromatic number. Reed's omega, delta, and chi
conjecture states that $$\chi(G) \leq \lceil \frac{1}{2}(\omega(G) + \Delta(G) + 1) \rceil.$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem reed_omega_delta_chi_conjecture :
  ∀ {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V),
    let χ := G.chromaticNumber
    let ω := G.ecliqueNum
    let Δ := G.emaxDegree
    2 * χ ≤ ω + Δ + 2 := by
  sorry

/--
For a finite graph $G$, we define $\Delta(G)$ to be the maximum degree, $\omega(G)$ to be the
size of the largest clique subgraph, and $\chi(G)$ to be the chromatic number. Reed's omega,
delta, and chi conjecture states that $$\chi(G) \leq \lceil \frac{1}{2}(\omega(G) + \Delta(G) + 1) \rceil.$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem reed_omega_delta_chi_conjecture_for_finite_graphs :
  ∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
    let χ := G.chromaticNumber
    let ω := G.cliqueNum
    let Δ := G.maxDegree
    2 * χ ≤ ω + Δ + 2 := by
  sorry

/--
The simplest open case is when $\Delta(G) = 6$ and $\omega(G) = 2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem reed_conjecture_Δ_6_ω_2 :
  ∀ {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V), G.emaxDegree = 6 ∧ G.cliqueNum = 2 → G.chromaticNumber ≤ 5 := by
    sorry

end ReedOmegaDeltaChi

reformulations.difference: Uses extended-natural graph invariants, quantifies over possibly infinite graphs, and states a doubled inequality rather than the usual finite-graph ceiling bound.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: On finite graphs, ecliqueNum and emaxDegree equal the natural clique number and maximum degree after coercion. Conversely, assume the finite conjecture. If either extended invariant is infinity, the displayed inequality is automatic. Otherwise write their values as natural numbers w and d. Every finite subgraph has clique number at most w and maximum degree at most d, hence is colorable with floor((w+d+2)/2) colors. Finite-subgraph compactness gives the same coloring bound for the whole graph. The integer rounding identity then gives the displayed inequality. The complete equivalence with the finite ceiling formulation was proved as Review.allReed_iff_finiteCeilingReed in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

For natural numbers c,w,d, 2*c ≤ w+d+2 iff c ≤ floor((w+d+2)/2), and this floor equals ceil((w+d+1)/2). Thus the extra 1 on the doubled right-hand side implements the ceiling exactly, rather than weakening the bound. A finite graph has finite chromaticNumber, and the decidability instances can be supplied classically. The full universally quantified equivalence was proved as Review.finiteReed_iff_finiteCeilingReed in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: Uses maximum degree exactly 6 and natural clique number exactly 2 on arbitrary graphs, whereas MathOverflow asks about triangle-free graphs with maximum degree at most 6.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For arbitrary simple graphs, cliqueNum = 2 is equivalent to triangle-freeness together with having an edge; this was proved directly from the definitions. In particular, the default cliqueNum = 0 for unbounded clique sizes cannot satisfy the hypothesis. Given any triangle-free graph of maximum degree at most 6, adjoining a disjoint K_{1,6} produces a triangle-free graph with maximum degree exactly 6 and clique number exactly 2. Restricting a 5-coloring recovers the original graph's coloring. The reverse implication is immediate, and finite-subgraph compactness equates the finite and unrestricted versions. Review.exactlySix_iff_finiteAtMostSix proves the complete equivalence in Lean.

review.notes: Checked all three declarations and found no mathematical defects or source-reported status changes. Wiley returned HTTP 403 for both the cited paper page and PDF, so the original paper's full text was unavailable; the two other cited sources explicitly state the claims and were read, including their remarks and comments. The final scratch file compiles successfully, and axiom checks confirm that the equivalence proofs do not depend on sorryAx. Boundary checks cover empty and singleton graphs, K2, infinite-graph default values, and the satisfiable special-case witness K_{1,6}; executable tests also confirm the rounding identity over small inputs and the star's degree and clique counts. The reviewed file matches the committed version exactly.
